business: Foley Eileen M., Lawyer (E. Foley Firm) - The Law Office of Eileen M. Foley, Esq., LLC

opportunities.title: Fix the front door: valid HTTPS, tap-to-call, machine-readable practice profile and consistent listings
opportunities.problem: Every visitor today hits a browser security warning or a dead end. The site only answers on plain HTTP; https://www.efoleyfirm.com/ fails with a self-signed certificate (net::ERR_CERT_AUTHORITY_INVALID), and the plain-HTTP copy was blocked by the reviewer's browser. The contact page has zero <form> elements and zero tel: links, so a phone visitor cannot tap to call and cannot submit an enquiry; the only email links in the header and footer are misspelled 'efole@efoleyfirm.com' (the correct address appears only in the page body). There is no meta description, no LocalBusiness/Attorney JSON-LD, and no East Brunswick in the title, so neither a search engine nor an AI assistant can reliably answer 'who is the family lawyer at 330 Milltown Rd' or book through it. Meanwhile the Google profile advertises 'Online appointments' with no booking path, holds zero reviews and no photos, and third-party directories still show North Brunswick addresses.
evidence: HTTPS fails with a self-signed certificate; site reachable only over plain HTTP, which the review browser refused to load (https://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

Contact page HTML contains no <form> and no tel: link; the header and footer 'Contact us' / 'Send an Email' links point to a misspelled mailto efole@efoleyfirm.com while the body shows efoley@efoleyfirm.com (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)
An empty <div class="form"> and a js/contact.js script are left in the contact page with no form fields underneath - the form scaffold was never finished (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)
<meta name="description"> is empty, no JSON-LD/schema markup anywhere, title names the counties but not East Brunswick, and leftover template slider code sits in the HTML (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)

Google Business Profile is categorised 'Family law attorney' with correct East Brunswick address and phone, but shows no star rating, no reviews, no photos, and attributes 'Online appointments' and 'Appointment required/recommended' that the website cannot fulfil (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)

Directory data disagrees with the firm's own page: Lawyers.com/Martindale show '1 Unknown, North Brunswick, NJ 08902' and Avvo shows a different North Brunswick firm's address; Yelp has no listing at all (https://www.avvo.com/attorneys/08902-nj-eileen-foley-1606317.html)
opportunities.agent_design: Three workstreams, one owner-approval gate. (1) Infrastructure: install a CA-issued certificate on the host, force 301 from http to https, fix the two misspelled mailto links, add a mobile sticky tap-to-call bar and a real consultation-request form with a server-side handler (the leftover js/contact.js scaffold shows the original form was never wired up). (2) Machine readability: LocalBusiness/Attorney JSON-LD with address, phone, hours, service-area counties and named towns, practice-area pages, and a readable meta description per page - so assistants and crawlers can extract and quote the firm. (3) Data hygiene agent: a scheduled agent that watches the TLS expiry date, broken links and 404s, then diffs the firm's canonical name/address/phone/hours against Google Business Profile, Avvo, Lawyers.com and Yelp, drafting the correction submissions and emailing the owner a weekly one-screen diff. The owner (or her assistant) approves every correction and every listing change; nothing is published or claimed without her click. Review flow: after a matter closes she marks it closed in the log, the agent drafts a plain review request for her to send from her own address - no automated posting, no solicitation inside an active matter.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A website builder subscription cannot fix a lapsed certificate on an existing host, redirect the HTTP copy, correct an inherited 2010s template, or keep four independent listings in sync. The value is in the last part: the work is monitoring and correction across systems that don't talk to each other (host/DNS, Google, Avvo/Martindale, Yelp), running unattended, with a weekly human-approved diff. A one-off web-designer invoice fixes the page once; the listings drift again within months.

impact_estimate.range: No revenue is claimed. Quantifiable effect: removal of the certificate interstitial that every visitor currently sees, plus roughly 1-3 hours/month of assistant or attorney time no longer spent repeating hours, address, fee policy and 'how do I start' by phone - about $360-$2,800/year of freed capacity - before any change in enquiry conversion, which is not measured and is not counted here.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, not sourced: (a) 1-3 hrs/month of phone/message time goes to routine logistics questions, based on the fact that the only published channel is a phone number with no FAQ, no form and no after-hours message path; (b) value of that time is priced at New Jersey legal-secretary median ($63,080/yr ~ $30/hr) up to New Jersey lawyer median ($161,430/yr ~ $78/hr) on 2,080 hours, 12 months; (c) no new clients, no new revenue and no ranking improvement are assumed, because client volume and conversion are unpublished. The larger, unquantified effect is that a client or an AI assistant following the Google 'Online appointments' attribute today reaches nothing.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 2 weeks: working CA certificate with http->https 301 (verified from a clean browser and a phone), fixed mailto links and tap-to-call bar, one wired consultation-request form that emails the firm and returns an auto-acknowledgement, Attorney/LocalBusiness JSON-LD plus meta descriptions on the six main pages, corrected name/address/phone/hours pushed to Google and to at least one stale directory, and a monitoring agent running weekly with a sample diff report.

opportunities.title: After-hours and court-day intake agent: capture, screen and book the free 15-minute call
opportunities.problem: The firm's only working channels are a phone number answered during Monday-Friday 9-5 and a mailto link. There is no form, no scheduler, no chat, no answering service and no after-hours message path, so every enquiry that arrives in the evening, at a weekend, or while the sole attorney is in family court has nowhere to land. Worse, the funnel is gated on live attorney time: the published process is a free 15-minute telephone consultation before any in-office consultation is scheduled, so the attorney personally screens each caller - including conflicts, venue and urgency questions - before a single billable matter exists. A testimonial credits 'her assistant', so a small staff absorbs part of this, but nothing records or routes what comes in.
evidence: Published hours Monday-Friday 9 AM-5 PM, closed Saturday and Sunday; Google lists 'Online appointments' and 'Appointment required/recommended' but the site has no scheduler or booking widget of any kind (https://www.google.com/maps/search/Eileen+Foley+lawyer+East+Brunswick+NJ)

Firm advertises a free 15-minute telephone consultation, with an in-office consultation fee credited against the first legal bill - i.e. an attorney-time screen precedes every matter (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/consultation.html)
Page HTML contains zero tel: links and zero <form> elements; the documented channels are phone 732-360-8116, email and fax 732-353-6879 (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)

The site states a client's matter 'will be handled start to finish by Ms. Foley' and a testimonial thanks 'her assistant' - so intake is answered by one attorney plus at least one support person, with no dedicated intake function (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/testimonials.html)
Practice mix includes domestic violence and DCP&P litigation, where first contact can be time-critical (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)
opportunities.agent_design: A written-and-voice intake agent that owns the first contact, with the attorney as the only approver of a booking. Triggers: web form submit, inbound email to the firm address, missed/after-hours call routed to a VoIP number, or a voicemail transcription. It captures a structured intake: caller identity and relationship to the opposing party (so a conflict pre-check can run against her matter list before she spends time), county/venue, matter type (divorce, custody/parenting time, support, alimony, relocation, post-judgment, DCP&P, domestic violence, guardianship, adoption), key dates and any emergency indicator. Domestic-violence and DCP&P contacts are escalated to the attorney's phone within minutes with a short summary; everything else gets an acknowledgement within minutes, a choice of open 15-minute phone slots from her calendar, and a booking that lands only after her approval (or inside her stated rules). It writes every contact into one shared inbox/CRM record with a timestamp, never gives legal advice, never quotes a fee beyond the published policy, and keeps transcripts in a tenant she controls. Weekly digest: contacts, bookings, declines, and anything it could not classify.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: A website chatbot or a Calendly link handles one channel and no judgement. This needs three integrations that don't exist yet (a phone/VoIP leg with transcription, her calendar, and a durable client-contact record), plus conflict pre-screening logic, an emergency escalation path, and an audit trail showing what the agent said and who approved each booking - which is what N.J. RPC 5.3 supervision of nonlawyer assistance and RPC 1.6 confidentiality actually require. Reliability matters more than fluency: measured legal-question hallucination and answer instability mean the agent must be retrieval-bound to her own intake script and must never answer a substantive legal question.

impact_estimate.range: $3,000-$18,000/year of freed attorney-and-assistant capacity (not cash), plus recovery of enquiries that today reach nothing. If two to five hours a week of combined intake handling shift off the attorney and her assistant, that is 96-240 hours a year at $30-$78/hour.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, not sourced: (a) 2-5 hrs/week of the attorney's and assistant's time goes to first-contact handling, re-calls and manual scheduling - plausible because every enquiry is a live 15-minute attorney screen with no form, booking tool or answering service; (b) 48 working weeks; (c) priced at the New Jersey legal-secretary median ($63,080, ~$30/hr) and lawyer median ($161,430, ~$78/hr) on 2,080 hours, uncorrected for the $350/hour figure on the third-party Avvo profile, which may be stale; (d) no recovered-client revenue is assumed because conversion and client volume are unpublished. Throughput evidence behind the design: automated intake routing reached 97.37% hits@2 on 419 real referral queries in a legal-aid setting (JURIX 2025 conference paper, not a journal article), and a generative-AI field experiment on support agents raised issues resolved per hour by 14% overall (NBER working paper 31161; reported as published in QJE 140(2) 2025, publication not independently verified here).

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks: an after-hours web form plus email triage and a booking flow with attorney approval on every appointment, live on one channel first (email + form) and then the missed-call path; a conflict pre-check field against a supplied matter list; a domestic-violence/DCP&P escalation rule tested against scripted scenarios; 30 days of transcripts reviewed with her to tune the script; a handover sheet of every contact with timestamps.

opportunities.title: Engagement-to-retainer pipeline with a client document portal (no more fax-and-chase)
opportunities.problem: Nothing between 'she said yes' and 'the first bill' is automated. There is no client portal, no document upload, no e-signature and no payment link anywhere on the site; the only transaction-adjacent channel is a fax number. Every new matrimonial matter therefore means someone assembling an engagement letter, a retainer invoice and a document checklist by hand, then chasing tax returns, pay stubs, account statements and custody schedules by phone or fax - work that falls on one attorney plus at least one assistant while the attorney is also the only person doing the legal work.
evidence: No client portal, document upload, payment link or e-signature mentioned anywhere on the site; the only transaction-adjacent channel listed is fax 732-353-6879 (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)

The site promises each matter 'will be handled start to finish by Ms. Foley' with one assistant credited by a testimonial - so engagement paperwork, retainer billing and document collection all queue behind the same two people (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/testimonials.html)

The contact page's only form is an empty <div class="form"> scaffold and a js/contact.js include - there is no form backend to send a document checklist or collect an upload (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html)
The published fee path is an in-office consultation fee credited against the first legal bill, so a retainer invoice is issued early in every matter (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/consultation.html)
Practice areas span divorce, custody, support, post-judgment applications and DCP&P litigation, each with a different opening document set (http://www.efoleyfirm.com/)
opportunities.agent_design: An agent-built pipeline that stitches together tools she does not have yet, with the attorney approving every document that leaves the office. On 'matter opened' it generates the engagement letter from her own Word template with matter-specific variables, assembles a retainer invoice at the amount she types, requests e-signature (DocuSign/Adobe Sign), and issues a retainer payment link through a trust-compliant processor (LawPay or equivalent) - amounts and trust disbursements are never agent-decided, and the agent has read-only access to balances. It then builds a matter-type document checklist (divorce: prior returns, pay stubs, account and retirement statements, deed; custody: schedules, school and medical records; DCP&P: agency letters and court papers), serves it on a secure upload page, and runs a chase agent that tracks which items arrived, reminds the client at set intervals, and escalates to the assistant after two reminders. Every generated document, approval and send is written to an immutable log so she can show who reviewed what. No filings, no court submissions, no client advice.
opportunities.why_not_DIY: Four regulated or sensitive systems have to work together: her document templates, e-signature, trust-compliant payments and secure file storage inside Microsoft 365 permissions. A generic form builder cannot touch a retainer invoice, cannot hold privilege-protected financial documents safely, and leaves no supervision trail. The builds that fail are the ones where an assistant-chatbot writes the letter and money moves - here the agent assembles and routes, and a human signs.

impact_estimate.range: $2,000-$7,000/year of assistant time recovered on engagement packets, checklists and document chasing (roughly 1.5-4 hours a week, 48 weeks, at $30-$34/hour), plus fewer unbilled callback cycles.
impact_estimate.assumptions: Inference, not sourced: (a) 1.5-4 hrs/week of assistant time goes to assembling engagement/retainer paperwork and chasing missing documents by phone and fax - plausible because there is no portal, no e-sign, no upload and no automated reminder path; (b) 48 working weeks; (c) priced at New Jersey legal-secretary median ($63,080, ~$30/hr) and paralegal median ($71,500, ~$34/hr) on 2,080 hours; (d) no reduction in attorney hours and no faster collection of retainers are counted, and no cash-flow improvement is claimed, because fee amounts, retainer sizes and matter volume are all unpublished.

opportunities.pilot_scope: 3-4 weeks on one matter type (divorce): engagement letter generated from her template, e-sign request, retainer invoice and payment link in test mode, a document checklist and secure upload page, reminder sequence with escalation to the assistant, and an approval log she signs off on - run against two live matters with her reviewing every outbound document before it sends.

lead_score.rationale: Pain (22/30): unusually clean, directly observed front-door evidence, independently confirmed twice - a self-signed certificate blocking HTTPS, zero <form> and zero tel: links on every page, a mailto misspelled in the header and footer, empty meta description, no schema, no booking despite Google advertising 'Online appointments', an unrated zero-review profile with no photos, and four directories that disagree on her address. That is a broken front door on a 35-year practice, so opportunity 1 (capability G) comes first: an agent on top of a site that cannot be opened safely does not help. Pain for opportunities 2 and 3 is absence-based rather than complaint-based - no public review mentions missed calls, scheduling or billing, so those two rest on the funnel design (free 15-minute attorney screen, 9-5 phone-only, fax as the only transaction channel), which caps pain below the top band. Fit (17/20): capabilities G, A, C and D all apply to one clearly identified decision maker with a simple static stack and no IT gatekeeper; the only fit gap is that no volume of matter work exists to automate. Ability to pay (11/20): a solo matrimonial practice with real retainers and a $350/hour figure published on Avvo (third-party, possibly stale), but one attorney, one suite shared with a CPA's office, a 2024 pro bono award and no revenue, matter-count or fee-schedule data - so a five-figure build is unlikely and a small, staged engagement is the realistic shape. Ease (12/15): the site is plain HTML on a single host, there is one approver, and the first pilot is two weeks of well-understood work; points off because she is deliberately referral-fed ('quality overrides quantity') and may not see a website as a business problem, so the sale, not the build, is the constraint. Strategic (13/15): the same pattern - solo or two-lawyer firm, lapsed certificate, no form or scheduler, stale directory addresses, no portal - repeats across thousands of New Jersey family, immigration, personal-injury and estate practices, so a front-door-plus-intake package productises cleanly. Physical/edge (capability E) was deliberately not included: no avenues.json was supplied, and this business is a single rented office suite (Suite W21 inside a multi-tenant professional building, listed as located in a CPA's office) with one attorney and one assistant, no inventory, equipment, fleet, shop floor or client-facing premises - there is nothing for a camera or sensor to observe, and the only surveillance-shaped use (office security) would add an alarm-business licensing burden under N.J.S.A. 45A:5A-2 for no operational gain. Evidence is not thin on the front-door facts; it is thin on the business side (no revenue, client counts, matter volume or fee schedule), which is why every dollar figure above is framed as recovered capacity rather than revenue and states its source and assumption.

best_evidence_signal: A referral-fed, 35-year family-law practice whose front door cannot be used: contact page has no form and no tel: link, its header and footer email links are misspelled 'efole@efoleyfirm.com', and the HTTPS copy fails on a self-signed certificate - http://www.efoleyfirm.com/contact.html
